findings.motion: SB 1174 (Min) Senate Third Reading, Assembly Floor; passed 57 ayes, 16 noes, 6 abstentions
findings.note: Voted aye on the Assembly floor for SB 1174, which bars local governments from enacting or enforcing voter identification requirements. Roll call taken from the Digital Democracy bill page; the official leginfo vote page was blocked.

findings.passage: “Proposition 39 is a tool to suppress voter participation, plain and simple. Donald Trump’s endorsement is proof enough of that,” Rivas and Limón said in a joint statement.
findings.note: Joint statement with the Senate leader, quoted by CALÓ News, about the 2026 voter ID initiative (Proposition 39), issued when they sued over its voter guide arguments. The article date is the date shown on the page.

findings.passage: "Don’t let anyone make you afraid to vote," said Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas, "don’t let anyone make it harder for your neighbor to vote, and don’t let Donald Trump bring his voter suppression agenda to California."
findings.note: Remarks at a campaign event against Proposition 39 (2026 voter ID initiative), quoted by KALW. Date is the article date.

findings.motion: Verified petition for writ of mandate, Rivas v. Weber (Sacramento Superior Court), challenging ballot arguments for Proposition 39
findings.note: He and the Senate leader filed a petition against the Secretary of State and State Printer to change the Proposition 39 voter guide arguments. The filing is stamped late July 2026; a news page says a judge later ruled for the petitioners.
